pr_title: Periodic warning for 1-node cluster w/ seed hosts
pr_body:
For fully-formed single-node clusters, emit a periodic warning if
seed hosts have been configured.

Closes #85222
pr_comments: Also I've added the `cloud-deploy` label, it would be good to confirm (manually) that this doesn't trigger any warnings on single-node Cloud clusters.

Hi @DaveCTurner , I've manually checked that the warning doesn't appear on a local distribution I built. How can I manually test it on a single-node cloud cluster? Does the cloud-deploy label somehow automatically spin a cloud cluster so I can check the logs?
Hi @DaveCTurner , also pushed suggested changes, please check once more.

> How can I manually test it on a single-node cloud cluster?

I shared a link to the internal docs in another channel.
@DaveCTurner please check once more and review.
Hi @DaveCTurner , PR is ready for your review.
:+1: sorry I'm unlikely to get to this today now, but it's on my list.

@DaveCTurner I was eager to merge this but I understand we want to make sure cloud sets the settings correctly :) 
By the way, when I tested it, I did see that seed_hosts was set to []. So the https://github.com/elastic/cloud-on-k8s/issues/5834 is to make sure it truly happens and it's not by chance?

@DaveCTurner  thinking more about this: The current condition for the warning is if the seed_hosts is set, and it is non-empty. I think the cloud uses either the file method (without the seed_hosts at all) or might set it to an empty list. So I think the current code should be OK for the cloud. Or do they populate seed_hosts for some reason for single-node clusters? (I remind we don't look now at all the last discovered hosts)
I think this works fine as-is in Cloud (i.e. ESS) but not in ECK.

@DaveCTurner , ah I see! I think ECK does not set seed_hosts at all, so they should not get the warning (as we do not look now for last discovered hosts -- which would include the unicast_hosts.txt file). I can test ECK with a single-node to confirm. Will try to see if they have instructions on testing.
Thanks @DaveCTurner ! By the way, I believe the issue https://github.com/elastic/cloud-on-k8s/issues/5834 might not be needed anymore with our new approach. Should we propose to close it?

No I think the ECK issue still has value even now. If a node cannot find the master then it will (eventually) emit log messages about all the addresses it's trying, which will include the default seed addresses if this setting isn't set, and that just causes confusing noise.
Ah, that's another message that gets emitted while trying to find masters. OK, thanks for the explanation! Will merge this when it passes the tests.

issue_context.title: More helpful logs if a single-node cluster has nontrivial discovery config
issue_context.body:
Users sometimes accidentally auto-bootstrap their nodes into single-node clusters and then try and join them all together later by setting `discovery.seed_hosts` or similar. Elasticsearch doesn't care if discovery points to a few extra nodes so today it reports no problems, but it's frustrating to the user that it doesn't do what they expect it to do and also doesn't indicate why.

It's almost certainly incorrect to have a nontrivial discovery config in a single-node cluster: `discovery.seed_hosts` and `discovery.seed_providers` should both be unset or empty[^1], so this is a strong indicator that the user is trying to form a multi-node cluster incorrectly. We can therefore be more helpful to these users by emitting periodic warnings in a single-node cluster with nontrivial discovery config:

> `This node is a fully-formed single-node cluster with cluster UUID [{clusterUUID}], but [{setting}] is set to [{value}] as if to discover other nodes and form a multi-node cluster. Fully-formed clusters do not attempt to discover other nodes, and nodes with different cluster UUIDs cannot belong to the same cluster. The cluster UUID persists across restarts and can only be changed by deleting the contents of the node's data path(s). Remove the discovery configuration to suppress this message.`

[^1]: it's also (kind of) acceptable if `discovery.seed_hosts` contains just the node's own publish address, or we're using just the `file` provider and `unicast_hosts.txt` contains just the node's own publish address.
comments: Is anybody working on this? If not can I take it?
Hi, @chen-ni , I have added the label by mistake, sorry for the confusion. This one has been assigned to @kingherc

Hi @DaveCTurner , in your original description you have given a footnote of a kind of valid/acceptable setting for the seed hosts, where the single-node cluster mentions its own public address. Should we take into consideration this acceptable setting? Or should we always emit the periodic warning when the seed hosts are non-empty, and hint to removing the setting (even in the valid/acceptable setting where the single-node cluster mentions itself)?
Unfortunately yes I think we must ignore our own address before checking for a nonempty seed hosts. In ESS and ECK and so on I believe one-node clusters will be configured to discover themselves.
@DaveCTurner thanks for the explanation! Finally, do we already store internally the cluster's own public address somewhere, so as to compare? Or should we figure it out programmatically?

You can get it by calling `getAddress()` on the `DiscoveryNode` object corresponding to the local node, which you can typically access via `transportService.getLocalNode()` or `clusterState.getNodes().getLocalNode()` (and probably many other paths too).

Hi @DaveCTurner ! In trying this case of a single-node cluster trying to join another one, I do see a warning already emitted:

> [2022-06-22T11:45:31,264][WARN ][o.e.c.c.Coordinator      ] [node_t0] failed to validate incoming join request from node [{other0}{KPOWduSVSsy5gNiA9TBbhQ}{HPOV9FTnRfeyU2tjiYkVMQ}{other0}{127.0.0.1}{127.0.0.1:13302}{cdfhilmrstw}]
org.elasticsearch.transport.RemoteTransportException: [other0][127.0.0.1:13302][internal:cluster/coordination/join/validate]
Caused by: org.elasticsearch.cluster.coordination.CoordinationStateRejectedException: This node previously joined a cluster with UUID [saM90swPSi-BOfsMybowqw] and is now trying to join a different cluster with UUID [3u784dcFRj2bG5P3aRZEIQ]. This is forbidden and usually indicates an incorrect discovery or cluster bootstrapping configuration. Note that the cluster UUID persists across restarts and can only be changed by deleting the contents of the node's data path [/tmp/org.elasticsearch.discovery.single.SingleNodeDiscoveryIT_FCD470C364EA96D8-001/tempDir-003/other0] which will also remove any data held by this node.
	at org.elasticsearch.cluster.coordination.JoinValidationService.lambda$new$2(JoinValidationService.java:130) ~[classes/:?]
	...

So, I do see already some warning message for the use case you mentioned. The warning message is different than the one you suggested, but with similar content. Are you aware of this warning message? Or is it a different use case?

@DaveCTurner  In figuring things out, the warning I posted earlier was when I was trying to join another cluster with cluster.initial_master_nodes rather than discovery.seed_hosts. So no need to reply. Will continue investigating and learning in the meantime.

That's right, as long as the node is actively trying to join a different cluster it will emit warnings like that. The trouble is when you have multiple single-node clusters that you expect to be a single multi-node cluster, you won't get any such warnings.

review_comments:
Settings must be registered in `ClusterSettings` otherwise they won't be accepted in the config file:

```diff
diff --git a/server/src/main/java/org/elasticsearch/common/settings/ClusterSettings.java b/server/src/main/java/org/elasticsearch/common/settings/ClusterSettings.java
index b225f6fb4ca..89d16c01df4 100644
--- a/server/src/main/java/org/elasticsearch/common/settings/ClusterSettings.java
+++ b/server/src/main/java/org/elasticsearch/common/settings/ClusterSettings.java
@@ -492,6 +492,7 @@ public final class ClusterSettings extends AbstractScopedSettings {
         ElectionSchedulerFactory.ELECTION_DURATION_SETTING,
         Coordinator.PUBLISH_TIMEOUT_SETTING,
         Coordinator.PUBLISH_INFO_TIMEOUT_SETTING,
+        Coordinator.SINGLE_NODE_CLUSTER_SEED_HOSTS_CHECK_INTERVAL_SETTING,
         JoinValidationService.JOIN_VALIDATION_CACHE_TIMEOUT_SETTING,
         FollowersChecker.FOLLOWER_CHECK_TIMEOUT_SETTING,
         FollowersChecker.FOLLOWER_CHECK_INTERVAL_SETTING,
```
